title: The Serapeum as a sonohydrogen plant

tellings.quote: ultrasound to break down water molecules to produce hydrogen and oxygen which is my hypothesis for the function of the sarapium.

plain: The Serapeum, an underground complex of tunnels and huge stone boxes at Saqqara in Egypt, was, in this theory, a plant that used ultrasound to break water molecules apart into hydrogen and oxygen. A guest named Geoffrey Drumm offers this as his own hypothesis, without naming a source. If true, the site would have been an ancient machine for making hydrogen.
